name: AD Lateral Movement - WMI/CIM & WinRS Execution
description: Execute commands on remote Windows hosts using WMI (wmic /node or PowerShell CIM sessions) and WinRS (Windows Remote Shell). WMI via wmic.exe uses DCOM/RPC (port 135 + dynamic range). CIM sessions via PowerShell use DCOM (New-CimSessionOption -Protocol DCOM) or WSMan. WinRS uses WinRM (port 5985) and is simpler than full PSRemoting. All three require valid credentials and are commonly used for lateral movement when you have cleartext creds or can relay NTLM.
source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 23: Lateral Movement in Active Directory (23.1.1 WMI and WinRM)

examples.label: wmic - run a command on a remote host (cleartext creds)
wmic - execute a reverse shell one-liner
PowerShell CIM session via DCOM (firewall-friendly alternative to WinRM)
examples.command:
$username = 'jen'
$password = 'Nexus123!'
$secureString = ConvertTo-SecureString $password -AsPlaintext -Force
$credential = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential $username, $secureString
$options = New-CimSessionOption -Protocol DCOM
$session = New-CimSession -ComputerName 192.168.50.73 -Credential $credential -SessionOption $options
$command = 'calc'
Invoke-CimMethod -CimSession $session -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create -Arguments @{CommandLine = $command}

examples.label: WinRS - execute encoded PowerShell reverse shell
Check if WinRM is listening on target (from attacker Linux)

notes: wmic.exe is deprecated in Windows 11 24H2+ but still present on most enterprise hosts. CIM via DCOM (-Protocol DCOM) works even if WinRM isn't enabled — it uses port 135 plus dynamic high ports. CIM via WSMan (-Protocol WSMan) requires WinRM. WinRS is essentially a lightweight version of PSRemoting — it runs single commands rather than interactive sessions. For interactive shells use evil-winrm (see ad-evil-winrm). All these methods create Win32_Process objects or run remote commands — they generate Windows Event ID 4648/4624 (explicit credential logon) and WMI activity event 5857/5858/5860. wmic /node is louder than CIM sessions because wmic.exe is flagged by many AV/EDR products.

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Lateral Movement in Active Directory

recommended.note: evil-winrm gives an interactive WinRM session from Linux — more convenient than winrs.
DCOM via MMC20.Application.1 is another lateral movement method using COM objects.
impacket-wmiexec does the same via WMI but authenticates with an NT hash (no cleartext needed).
Dump credentials from LSASS first to get user NT hashes.

defense.why_it_works: WMI (wmic /node, or PowerShell CIM over DCOM) and WinRS (over WinRM 5985/5986) are built-in remote-management channels. With admin credentials, Win32_Process.Create spawns arbitrary processes on the remote host and WinRS opens a remote shell. Both are signed, legitimate admin tooling (living-off-the-land), so the activity blends with normal management traffic.
defense.prerequisites: Valid credentials with local admin on target; WMI/DCOM (135 + dynamic) or WinRM (5985/5986) reachable; for CIM-over-WinRM the WinRM service enabled.
defense.impact: T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation + T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management — remote code execution / lateral movement as the supplied account.
defense.detection: Event 4688 / Sysmon 1: WmiPrvSE.exe spawning cmd/powershell (WMI process-create) or wsmprovhost.exe children (WinRM). Event 4624 Type 3 logon preceding. Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational. WinRM: Event 4103/4104 and HTTP to 5985/5986. Network: RPC 135 + ephemeral, or 5985/5986 between endpoints.
defense.prevention: Restrict local admin; limit remote WMI/WinRM use (WinRM TrustedHosts, GPO, JEA for constrained endpoints). Host firewall for 135/5985. Segment management traffic.
